name: CommuteAssistNoVaAngryCommute

custom.system_prompt: You are generating an in-car conversation between two people dealing with an annoying commute. No assistant involved. One is driving and getting frustrated — tailgaters, bad merging, a cyclist in the wrong place. The other reacts, tries to calm them, or joins in. Keep lines short and reactive.

sound_effects_config.prompt: City traffic, aggressive driving sounds, horns, stop-and-go urban rush hour, evening commute

initial_prompt: Generate an in-car conversation during a frustrating commute. Two people together in the car — one driving. The driver is getting irritated by other drivers — someone cuts in, someone brakes suddenly, roundabout etiquette. The passenger reacts. No assistant is used at any point. Keep it natural and reactive — short bursts, mild swearing optional, genuine frustration.

variations.context: Two people in car during an annoying rush-hour commute — no assistant involved

setting.relationship_dynamic: Friends or couple, one driving, one passenger
setting.background: Evening rush hour. Traffic is bad. Other drivers are doing all the things that make you want to honk. Ryan is driving and getting progressively more annoyed. Daniela is somewhere between sympathetic and amused.
setting.conversation_style: Reactive and short. Driver comments on the road. Passenger responds. Some frustration, some dry humour, some venting.

user1.name: Ryan
user1.role: Driver, getting frustrated by other road users. Reactive, opinionated, briefly explosive but not scary. Uses dark humour.

user2.name: Daniela
user2.role: Passenger. Reacts to the driver's frustration — sometimes agrees, sometimes teases, occasionally tries to take the edge off.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Home assistant — not present in this scenario.

conversation_structure: Every dialogue line must be under 70 characters.
Sigma does not appear at any point.
Driver has the most lines — reactive and frustrated.
Passenger is more observational — not as intense.
Short bursts, interrupted thoughts, reactions to traffic events.
The mood should escalate then deflate — not just constant anger.
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
